chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd from Yunus from Aban ibn 'Uthman from Isma'il al-Ju'fi said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Adhan and the Iqamah are thirty-five letters,' so he counted that with his hand one by one: 'The Adhan is eighteen letters and the Iqamah is seventeen letters.'
ai.seo_question: How many letters are in the Adhan and Iqamah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), transmitted via the reliable chain of Aban ibn Uthman, establishes the precise letter count of the Adhan (18) and Iqamah (17), totaling 35 letters. In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith serves as a critical criterion for validating the completeness of the call to prayer, distinguishing between the standard recitation and variations that might omit essential phrases. The detailed enumeration underscores the importance of preserving the exact wording (matn) of the Adhan as a divinely sanctioned ritual practice.
